open_points.subject: activate_flow on unknown flow/version reference
open_points.text: A06 defines refusal for unproven/effectful-agent cases but does not state what happens when the named flow or flow version does not exist (e.g., "Activating a flow version proves it again first; an unproven version is refused").
open_points.question: If activation is requested for a non-existent flow_id or flow_version_id, is the refusal `unknown reference`, `unproven`, or another failure?
options: Refuse as unknown reference before proof
Treat as unproven proof failure
Return one generic refusal without distinguishing
open_points.default_guess: Refuse as unknown reference before any proof logic.

open_points.subject: unknown-outcome resolution with outputs (`applied_outputs_unknown`)
open_points.text: A11: "the element counts as failed with reason `applied_outputs_unknown`" while "the attempt's one NodeExecution keeps `outcome_unknown`" and A13 failure logic is mostly tied to NodeExecution statuses.
open_points.question: Where is `applied_outputs_unknown` represented for later checks/readers, and exactly how do dependants detect this as failed if NodeExecution status remains `outcome_unknown`?
options: Derive virtual failure from EffectAttempt+NodeExecution pair at read/advance time
Write an additional synthetic NodeExecution status
Store a separate per-element conclusion field on Run
open_points.default_guess: Derive virtual failure from the two records during run advancement and trace reads.

open_points.subject: approval status after crash with in-flight attempt
open_points.text: A11 rule 1: "recovery also marks that approval `used`" for crash between in-flight and outcome; A11 rule 4 describes startup conversion `in_flight -> unknown` but does not restate approval transition.
open_points.question: On restart recovery of `in_flight` attempts, must linked approvals always be moved to `used`, and at what exact step?
options: Always mark linked approval `used` when `in_flight` becomes `unknown`
Leave approval unchanged until owner resolves unknown
Mark `used` only if send had certainly started
open_points.default_guess: Mark linked approval `used` during `in_flight -> unknown` recovery.

open_points.subject: manifest path placeholder parsing
open_points.text: A09 rule 2 uses "every `{name}` in the path" but does not define placeholder grammar/escaping boundaries in State 2.
open_points.question: What exact parser defines placeholders in declared paths (e.g., nested braces, unmatched braces, literal braces)?
options: Simple `{identifier}` token scan with refusal on malformed braces
RFC6570-style template parsing
No placeholders unless exact whole-segment `{name}`
open_points.default_guess: Use strict whole-token `{name}` parsing and refuse malformed brace patterns.

open_points.subject: size checks for `many` values against `stored_value_bytes_max`
open_points.text: A04/A12 require each value to be within `stored_value_bytes_max`, and `many` values are arrays, but do not fully spell whether the limit applies to whole array bytes, each element, or both.
open_points.question: For a `many` value port, which byte size is enforced for `stored_value_bytes_max`?
options: Canonical JSON bytes of the whole array only
Per-element only
Both whole-array and per-element
open_points.default_guess: Enforce on the whole serialized value (array) as one StoredValue.

open_points.subject: contract violation attribution at edge validation
open_points.text: A13 rule 3: "A value is validated against the source port when it is produced and against the target port before it enters a node; a violation concludes the producing node, or the receiving node, `contract_violation`".
open_points.question: If both source-side and target-side validations could fail for the same transferred value, which node is deterministically blamed and recorded first?
options: Always source-side first at production time
Always target-side on consumption
Whichever check runs first in executor implementation
open_points.default_guess: Source-side failure wins because production validation occurs before delivery.

open_points.subject: split between A08 record checks and A09 instance checks
open_points.text: A08 rule 6 says send-time stale checks use "rule 5's checks of the record itself — not those of the instance, which are A09 rule 6's own", but A08 rule 5 itself includes instance-related conditions (selected instance/api_base_url/duplicate required header names).
open_points.question: Which exact checks are performed under A08 rule 6 versus deferred to A09 rule 6 at send time?
options: Treat instance selection/header-name duplication as A09-only pre-send checks
Repeat those instance checks in both A08 rule 6 and A09 rule 6
Restrict A08 rule 6 strictly to capability-entry checks plus digest match
open_points.default_guess: Restrict A08 rule 6 to capability-entry/invocability/digest checks; run instance/address/credential checks in A09 rule 6.
